Details: The test `testGenerateURLFragment` checks whether HTML entities such as `"` are correctly escaped to their corresponding character by the `StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment` method. ```java
78 :     public void testCompressedHeaderWithNonDefaultDictionarySize() throws Exception {
79 :         SevenZFile sevenZFile = new SevenZFile(getFile("COMPRESS-256.7z")); // error occurred here

```

```

	at org.tukaani.xz.LZMAInputStream.initialize(Unknown Source)

	at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.<init>(SevenZFile.java:94)
	at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFile.<init>(SevenZFile.java:116)
	at org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.sevenz.SevenZFileTest.testCompressedHeaderWithNonDefaultDictionarySize(SevenZFileTest.java:79)
```

The error reported by the test `testCompressedHeaderWithNonDefaultDictionarySize` indicates an `UnsupportedOptionsException` raised by the LZMAInputStream due to a dictionary size that is too large for this implementation. This occurs in the constructor of `SevenZFile` when reading encoded headers using the LZMADecoder.

The relevant methods in the `SevenZFile` class covered by the failing test include: constructors (`.SevenZFile(java.io.File, byte[])` and `.SevenZFile(java.io.File)`) as well as header-reading methods such as `.readHeaders(byte[])` and `.readEncodedHeader(...)`.

To diagnose the problem, the next step is to inspect the code snippet for the constructor `SevenZFile(java.io.File)` to see how the archive file is processed initially and how the headers are read. This step will provide insights into how the LZMA dictionary size parameter is handled or passed to the decoder.
